subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core global agent dry-run mode, and which execution surfaces must be covered before users can trust it as a safety boundary?
rationale: Automation can prove the current gap, but it cannot choose whether adapter-only interception is acceptable or whether Gateway, client-hosted, CLI-backend, and Codex-native tools must be included from day one.

options.title: Design the safety contract first
options.body: Specify supported surfaces, preview/result shape, and bypass behavior, then implement only the covered mode with tests proving no side effects through those paths.

options.title: Fold into broader safe modes
options.body: Track the work under the Ask/Plan/Modify direction while keeping this issue as the focused requirement for tool-call preview semantics.

options.title: Decline global interception
options.body: Keep per-command dry-runs and plugin policy hooks as the supported safety tools, then close this direction after maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design the safety contract first
recommendation.body: Specify supported surfaces, preview/result shape, and bypass behavior, then implement only the covered mode with tests proving no side effects through those paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The clearest older history signal on central agent command and execution helper surfaces points to this owner for the product/security contract decision.
